messages:
Maya Chen: quick heads-up — bringing up hybrid-embed-v2 (512d) with per-channel int8 quant. ran the multilingual holdout sweep (en,fr,es,zh) and seeing a surprising recall@1 drop vs fp16 baseline, esp for zh and fr.

Jonah Park: rough numbers?

Maya Chen: paste from the run (internal run: run_2026_03_hybv2_qint8):
```
baseline fp16: recall@1=0.842, recall@5=0.951, silhouette=0.27
per-channel int8: recall@1=0.799, recall@5=0.934, silhouette=0.21
zh subset: fp16 R@1=0.81 -> int8 R@1=0.70
fr subset: fp16 R@1=0.85 -> int8 R@1=0.77
```

Sophia Rivera: that's a ~4.3% absolute loss overall at R@1. Any difference in normalization or metadata handling in the quant pipeline?

Maya Chen: double-checked. We used the same normalization (L2) and the serialization path is identical. Differences are in quant kernel (per-channel symmetric) + OPQ not applied in the int8 path yet. Also KV-cache irrelevant for embeddings.

Ravi Patel: did you try per-tensor int8 for a quick compare? sometimes per-channel can amplify noise on smaller vocab subspaces.

Maya Chen: ran per-tensor too — slightly better than per-channel in this case but still down vs fp16:
```
per-tensor int8: recall@1=0.812, recall@5=0.941
```

Maya Chen: uMAP plots attached in the run artifacts show cluster elongation for zh queries — centroid drift toward other language clusters.

onboard-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/run_2026_03_hybv2_qint8/umap_multilang.png

Jonah Park: could be a side-effect of quant scale estimation on outlier dims. Did you compute per-dim dynamic range and kurtosis across languages?

Maya Chen: yes — zh embeddings have a heavier tail on dims 320-360. kurtosis ~ 5.6 vs 2.3 for en. scaling clamps in per-channel path are truncating those tails.

Sophia Rivera: two quick experimental suggestions: 1) try OPQ (rotation) before quant to redistribute variance, 2) calibration per-language or per-subset quant stats. Also run recall with cosine rescaling (temp) perhaps the similarity surface shifted.

Ravi Patel: agree. Also try per-channel asymmetric quant (zero-point) — may keep tail info. If OPQ + asymmetric helps, we can add to the quant recipe.

Maya Chen: next steps I'm running: OPQ (k=64) + per-tensor asymmetric, a language-specific calibration pass, and a small re-eval with nearest-neigh k=1/5/10 across 10k holdout. I'll post numbers. ETA ~ 3h.

Jonah Park: can you also dump a tiny diagnostics table: mean cosine shift by language for top-k true positives? helps prioritize.|

Maya Chen: will do. quick diff after OPQ run (prelim):
```
OPQ + per-tensor asymmetric: recall@1=0.834, recall@5=0.948, zh R@1=0.80, fr R@1=0.84
mean cosine shift (abs) pre->post: en=0.012, fr=0.038, zh=0.054
```

Sophia Rivera: promising — OPQ recovered most of the loss. We should surface a checklist for model onboarding: 1) check per-dim kurtosis, 2) try OPQ rotations, 3) compare per-tensor vs per-channel asymmetric, 4) language holdouts and calibration. Add to the onboarding doc.

Maya Chen: adding checklist to the run notes and will open a tiny PR to the onboarding guide. Also flagging this as a caution for default per-channel recipes on multilingual models.

Ravi Patel: thanks — if OPQ path looks stable, we should run QA evals (regression tests) on other datasets (semantic-sim, clustering) before promoting to dedicated-serving config.

Maya Chen: agreed. I'll run cross-dataset sweep overnight and post a summary tomorrow morning. :coffee:
